title: Selling Plans — Insertion Fees and the Monthly Listing Allowance
content:
**Rule.** On **Selling Plans**, every new listing and every automatic renewal of a listing counts once against the plan's zero-insertion allowance of the calendar month it is created or renewed in. Listings up to the allowance are booked at 0.00; each listing beyond it is booked at the plan's insertion fee after allowance. The allowance is the plan held on the day the listing is created; an unused allowance never carries into the next month.

## How a listing is priced

The count for a listing is the number of insertion fee records of the plan for the same calendar month (first to last day inclusive) booked before the listing being priced.

| Listings already booked this calendar month, before this one | Insertion fee booked for this listing |
|---|---|
| Fewer than the plan's monthly allowance | USD 0.00 |
| Equal to or more than the plan's monthly allowance | The plan's insertion fee after allowance |

Each insertion fee record shows the listing number, the date the listing was created or renewed, the calendar month it counts against and the amount (0.00 within the allowance).

## Boundary, shown on both sides (hypothetical plan with an allowance of 1000 listings a month)

- The 1000th listing of the month has 999 listings booked before it: fewer than 1000, so it is booked at USD 0.00.
- The 1001st listing of the month has 1000 listings booked before it: not fewer than 1000, so it is booked at the plan's insertion fee after allowance.

## Points of judgement

- **Renewals.** A listing that renews automatically counts again, in the calendar month it renews in.
- **Unused allowance.** A seller who used 600 of a 1000-listing allowance in May starts June with 1000, not 1400.
- **Which plan's allowance.** The allowance applied is that of the plan held on the day the listing is created.
